title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Confidentiality of Public Information
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: The outcome of a paralegal's recent Human Rights Tribunal hearing is published on CanLII and reported in the local newspaper. Is the paralegal now free to discuss the client's personal details with friends at a dinner party?
options: Yes, because the information is now in the public domain and no longer confidential.
No, the ethical duty of confidentiality survives even when information becomes part of the public record, and the paralegal should avoid casual discussions of client affairs.
Yes, as long as the paralegal does not profit from telling the story.
No, unless the friends sign a non-disclosure agreement.
questions.explain: Rule 3.03 states that the duty of confidentiality applies to all information concerning the client's affairs acquired in the course of the relationship. The duty continues indefinitely. Furthermore, the LSO guidelines clarify that a licensee should avoid discussing a client's affairs to satisfy curiosity, even if the facts are a matter of public record.
